I found this coin in my apartment complex's parking lot and I'm wondering if it's real or not as I have no experience identifying ancient Roman coins at all. Coin

I found it this morning while walking out to my car to go to work, it was on the ground between my neighbor's two cars parked in tandem. I instantly recognized it as a Roman coin but have no idea whether it's authentic or not.

It's shiny because it's been pretty heavily cleaned. You can see the pit marks on a few places, I imagine if you examined it closely you would find scratches as well.

As for authenticity I'm not familiar enough with ancient coins to make a call on that.

Being legit is not out of the realm of possibility. Some Roman coins are actually pretty cheap for how old they are. It may have been a carry piece that slipped out of a pocket. Or perhaps it got caught up in a book or something and fell out on its way to someone's car.

The off center strike and wonky lettering correlates to the methods of that time period. But those things are easily faked as well.

Hopefully someone with more knowledge of ancient coins will pop up.

That is a Denarius. If legit, it would have been struck under Emperor Tiberius between AD 14 and AD 37. Somtimes this particular coin is known as a Tribute Penny.

Once again, if legit, may be worth $700-$1000.
